Maya: quick heads up — after yesterday's hygiene sweep I see ~1.2k contacts with owner=null. looks like the playbook short-circuit rule we added for inbound-template suppression might be skipping claim flow :thinking_face:
Alex: oof. any example query or filter that triggered it?
Maya: yep — filtering by `source=marketing && last_touch < now()-90d` then we early-return if `has_template=true`. that early-return also skips owner assignment. snippet:
```sql
SELECT id, email, owner_id, source, last_touch, has_template
FROM contacts
WHERE source = 'marketing' AND last_touch < now() - interval '90 days' AND has_template = true;
```
Priya: hmm that's the short-circuit we added to avoid noisy playbook runs. we intended to skip routing for templates, not block owner backfill.
Jordan: can we make it two-phased? i.e. record candidate list then apply suppression only to playbook actions, not owner_claim job. minimal change: move early-return below owner_claim call.
Maya: agree. quick fix might be to flip order, but we should also run a dry-run backfill to validate.
Alex: i'll open a tiny PR to change execution order, add a unit test that ensures owner_claim runs even when has_template=true.
Priya: also recommend we add telemetry: increment `suppression_skipped_owner` metric when suppression would have blocked owner assignment so we catch regressions.
Maya: logging + metric sounds good. can we also run a one-off backfill to claim owners for those 1.2k contacts?
Jordan: sql for backfill looks like:
```sql
WITH candidates AS (
  SELECT id FROM contacts WHERE owner_id IS NULL AND last_touch < now() - interval '90 days' AND source = 'marketing'
)
UPDATE contacts SET owner_id = next_owner() FROM candidates WHERE contacts.id = candidates.id;
```
Alex: flag: `next_owner()` uses round-robin; we should cap rate so we don't flood CSM inboxes. add batching and `notify=false` for dry run.
Priya: propose dry-run today, small batch tomorrow (100/day) then ramp. i'll own scheduling.
Maya: tagging @Jordan and @Alex to coordinate PR + dry-run. can cs-bot run a lint and runbook check? :pray:
cs-bot: CI queued for PR #4281. runbook linter: found missing entry for `suppression_skipped_owner` metric — please add to ops/runbooks/owner-claims.md
Alex: noted — will add runbook blurb and the metric.
Jordan: timeline?
Maya: PR by EOD, dry-run tonight with `notify=false`, monitor metrics and slack alerts, full slow backfill starting tomorrow morning if green.
Priya: adding calendar block for runbook watch (2 hours) and will post results to #customer-health after dry-run. :white_check_mark:
Alex: PR link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/cs-tools/pull/4281
Maya: thanks — if anyone spots edge cases (e.g., templates tied to paywall accounts) call it out here. I'll coordinate rollback plan. :eyes:
Jordan: leaving a quick note — let's also add a sanity check exclude for `account_status = 'suspended'` to avoid claiming weird accounts.
Maya: good call. i'll update the backfill SQL.
Priya: all set from ops side. will post results in the morning.
Maya: closing loop once backfill is done. :rocket:
